text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Former foreign minister Povilas Gylys criticised the remarks of parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis in Brussels that there was no difference between NATO membership now or later. Gylys said this was making concessions to Russia.
- A raid on the warehouses of one of the biggest alcohol importers, Bennet Distributors, disclosed no violations.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas left for a two-day official visit to Kazakhstan.
- The average salary in Lithuania was $172, in Latvia $239 and $232 in the 3rd quarter in Estonia in January, the statistics department says.
- Jonas Kazlauskas, 42, former coach of the star team Zhalgiris, was chosen to train the national basketball team.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius told a news conference that the decision to compensate savings expropriated by the Soviet power will help to preserve social stability.
- Communications Minister Rimantas Pleikys said that the Vilnius radio and television transmitting centre should be privatised together with Lithuanian Telecom.

- The prosecutor's office should not be superior to the courts, said Minister of Justice Vytautas Pakalnishkis in the interview to the newspaper. A candidate to the prosecutor's post was vetoed by President Brazauskas on Wednesday.
- The Bank of New York intends to issue $9.9 million credit to Ignalina nuclear power plant .

- News agency BNS protested over the 300,000 litas contract ELTA news agency signed with parliament and the board of parliament decided to declare an open competition to choose a supplier of information of foreign news agencies.

- Banks may find themselves skating on thin ice as the government's war againt tax-dodgers heats up. Banks are required to report clients to the interior ministry who make large payments and transactions in cash.
